title: Fast and Inexpensive DNA and RNA Extraction from Plant and Fungal Samples
author: Peter W Inglis
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tzfep3n
materials: Gently suspend pellets in 100 µl TE containing 0.1 mg ml-1 DNase-free RNase A and incubate tubes at 37 °C for 30 minutes. DNA extraction notes: DNA purity may be conveniently estimated using a spectrophotometer, such as a Nanodrop 2000 (Thermo Scientific). DNA yield is more accurately estimated using a fluorimeter and fluorescent DNA binding dye, such as the Qubit system (Thermo Scientific). Yield may also be verified and DNA integrity checked by agarose gel electrophoresis. For applications requiring high yields and high molecular weight genomic DNA, such as long read single molecule PacBio sequencing, several grams of fresh tissue should be macerated with a mortar and pestle in the presence of liquid nitrogen. The extraction protocol is scaled up to use 15-ml or 50-ml tubes or several microtubes in parallel and the DNA consolidated at the end. Gentle handling must be adopted throughout the entire procedure with no or only minor vortexing and never any repeated pipetting. Resuspension of the tissue macerate following the sorbitol pre-washes should be carried out gently using a spatula and the final DNA precipitate recovered using a glass hook. DNA integrity can be estimated using pulsed-field gel electrophoresis and the adequate fraction selected for downstream sequencing using the Blue pippin DNA size selection system (BluePippin; Sage Science).
The supernatant is aspirated from samples and discarded.

steps.title: Perform sorbitol wash
steps.instruction: Add an excess of sorbitol wash buffer to each tube containing macerated plant material until the tube is about ¾ full (≈0.9–1.5 ml depending on tube size). Cap and shake the tubes in a bead mill, vortex, or manually until the powder is fully suspended; inspect and repeat shaking if needed.

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 2,500 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature. Decant or aspirate the supernatant and discard it.

steps.title: Optional repeat sorbitol wash
steps.instruction: If the discarded supernatant is highly turbid or viscous, repeat the sorbitol‑wash step (add buffer, shake, centrifuge) once more; usually one wash is sufficient.

steps.title: Add pre‑warmed extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Add pre‑warmed extraction buffer to each tube to roughly half the tube capacity (≈500–700 µl for 1.1 ml microtubes).

steps.title: Resuspend macerate
steps.instruction: Resuspend the macerated material by shaking for 5 seconds in the bead mill or by vortexing; the ball bearings aid mixing.

steps.title: Incubate at 65 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes at 65 °C for a minimum of 30 minutes and up to 60 minutes, inverting the tubes every 10 minutes. After incubation, allow the tubes to cool at room temperature for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add chloroform‑isoamyl alcohol (CIA)
steps.instruction: Add CIA (≈700 µl or enough to fill ~4/5 of the tube) to each tube and shake vigorously for 10 seconds (bead mill can be used).

steps.title: Centrifuge to separate phases
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 2,500 × g for 10 minutes at room temperature (do not exceed this speed to avoid tube rupture).

steps.title: Recover aqueous phase (optional second extraction)
steps.instruction: Carefully pipette the upper aqueous phase to a new tube, avoiding the interphase debris. If desired, repeat the extraction with an equal volume of fresh CIA, mix with the bead mill, and centrifuge at 2,500–13,000 × g for 10 minutes, then recover the aqueous phase again.

steps.title: Precipitate nucleic acids with acetate and isopropanol
steps.instruction: To the recovered aqueous phase add 1/10 volume of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) and 0.66 volume of cold isopropanol (stored at –20 °C). Invert the tube ten times and incubate at –20 °C for at least 1 hour or overnight.

steps.title: High‑speed centrifugation of precipitate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 13,000 × g for 10 minutes at room temperature (use the maximum allowable speed for a 96‑well plate rotor if applicable).

steps.title: Decant supernatant and drain tubes
steps.instruction: Carefully decant the supernatant and rest the tubes inverted on paper towels to drain any remaining liquid.

steps.title: Ethanol wash of pellet
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml of 70 % ethanol to each pellet, then centrifuge at 13,000 × g for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Remove ethanol supernatant
steps.instruction: Aspirate the ethanol supernatant carefully, taking care not to disturb the loose pellet.

steps.title: Dry pellet
steps.instruction: Dry the open tubes at room temperature for approximately 1 hour, or place them in a vacuum dryer for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Clean and reuse ball bearings (optional)
steps.instruction: Recover ball bearings with a sieve, wash with tap water, soak in 10 % bleach for 10 minutes, rinse four times with Milli‑Q water, and dry at 70 °C for at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Keep samples frozen for RNA extraction
steps.instruction: Maintain all biological material frozen until the sorbitol‑wash step; tubes can be frozen at –80 °C with the bead‑mill block, but thawing may occur during maceration.

steps.title: Prepare RNase‑free mortar and pestle
steps.instruction: Clean mortar, pestle, and spatula with an RNase‑decontamination solution, rinse with distilled water, dry, and pre‑chill in liquid nitrogen before grinding tissue.

steps.title: Pre‑heat water bath and lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Pre‑heat a water bath or incubator to 65 °C and warm the CTAB lysis buffer at 65 °C for at least 15 minutes before use.

steps.title: Transfer frozen macerate to tubes
steps.instruction: While keeping tissue frozen (liquid N₂ or dry ice), transfer macerated samples into 2.0 ml tubes (if not using the bead mill).

steps.title: First sorbitol wash for RNA
steps.instruction: Immediately add an excess of sorbitol wash buffer to fill each tube to about ¾ capacity (0.9–1.5 ml), cap, and shake (bead mill, vortex, or manually) until the powder is fully suspended; inspect and repeat shaking if needed.

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard supernatant (RNA)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 2,500 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Second sorbitol wash for RNA
steps.instruction: Repeat the sorbitol‑wash step (add buffer, shake, centrifuge) once more; two washes are routinely sufficient for RNA extraction.

steps.title: Add pre‑warmed CTAB extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Add 1.0 ml of pre‑warmed CTAB extraction buffer to each tube, shake vigorously, and place the tubes in a 65 °C water bath. Typical tissue amounts are ~100 µg leaf material or ~80 mg cambium per tube.

steps.title: Add chloroform and mix
steps.instruction: Add approximately 750 µl of chloroform to each tube and shake vigorously.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 10 minutes. Carefully aspirate the upper aqueous phase and transfer it to a fresh tube.

steps.title: Second chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Add 750 µl chloroform to the transferred aqueous phase, shake vigorously, and centrifuge again at 12,000 × g for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase and note volume
steps.instruction: Transfer the aqueous phase to a fresh tube and record the recovered volume.

steps.title: Add LiCl₂:EDTA on ice
steps.instruction: Place the tubes on ice and add an equal volume of LiCl₂:EDTA solution; mix well.

steps.title: Precipitate RNA at –20 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture for 2–4 hours at –20 °C (or overnight at 4 °C) to precipitate RNA.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet RNA
steps.instruction: Balance the tubes and centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully remove and discard the supernatant, taking care not to lose the RNA pellet.

steps.title: Dissolve pellet in SSTE
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 500 µl or 1000 µl SSTE (depending on pellet size). If needed, heat at 65 °C for 2–10 minutes to aid dissolution, then transfer to a fresh microtube.

steps.title: Chloroform extraction of dissolved RNA
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl chloroform, shake or vortex, and centrifuge at full speed for 5–7 minutes.

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Transfer the upper aqueous phase to a new microtube.

steps.title: Ethanol precipitation of RNA
steps.instruction: Add 2 volumes of 95 % ethanol to the aqueous phase and precipitate for at least 15 minutes at –80 °C.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet RNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at full speed for 20 minutes to pellet the RNA, then discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Ethanol wash of RNA pellet
steps.instruction: Add 200 µl cold 70 % ethanol, centrifuge at full speed for 3–5 minutes, and carefully aspirate the supernatant (pellet is loose after this wash).

steps.title: Air‑dry RNA pellet
steps.instruction: Lean the tubes open on their sides on the bench and air‑dry; do not use a speed‑vac to avoid contamination.

steps.title: Resuspend RNA in RNase‑free water or TE
steps.instruction: Add sterile RNase‑free Milli‑Q water or TE to dissolve the dried pellet (typically 10–50 µl depending on pellet size).
